newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria parliament debates CA sale.
newsitem.headline: Austria parliament debates CA sale.

text.p: Austria's parliament convened in special session on Tuesday to debate the sale of Creditanstalt to the country's biggest bank, Bank Austria.

The government of Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel's conservatives struck a last-minute deal at the weekend on the privatisation after a row over the purchaser had split the coalition.

Before Saturday's crisis coalition meeting, Schuessel's People's Party had held a series of talks with the far-right opposition Freedom Party over the bank sale and they had threatened to vote together to oppose the sale.

Both parties together can command an overall majority in parliament and such action could have seriously embarrassed the Social Democrats, who had backed the bid by Bank Austria to take over Creditanstalt, the country's number two bank.
But the coalition deal removed the threat of the conservatives and the Freedom Party mounting a joint attack on Vranitzky's party.
Schuessel won concessions from the Social Democrats in the deal, including a buyout of small Creditanstalt shareholders by Bank Austria and guarantees of job security for Creditanstalt employees.
